artists.name: Kate Lavender
artists.bio: Based in Keswick, Kate Lavender established North Lakes Stained Glass in 2021, drawing inspiration from the Lake District's emotive landscapes and nature. With over 30 years of experience in Tiffany foiling and lead light techniques, she creates unique pieces using reclaimed and textured glass. Her work, recently featured on BBC's Make It At Market, includes bespoke commissions, restoration, and creative workshops.

works.title: Red Roses
works.description: Six stained-glass red roses with green leaves, displayed in a dark green glazed vase.

works.title: Orange Tulips
works.description: Six stained-glass orange tulips with green leaves, displayed in a blue ceramic vase.

works.title: Orchid
works.description: Blush-toned stained-glass orchid stem with deep green leaves.

works.title: Green Mosaic Flower
works.description: Layered green stained-glass mosaic flower set on a cork round.

works.title: Exhibition Display
works.description: Exhibition display featuring Kate's tulips and mixed stained-glass stems alongside her artist statement.

artists.name: Angela Strange
artists.bio: Angela's ceramics are inspired by the natural world and rooted in domestic use. She makes functional ware with a focus on form, surface and quiet daily ritual. Wood firing is one part of that practice, bringing atmosphere, ash and unpredictability that leaves a distinctive mark on each piece.

works.title: Wood-fired teapot
works.description: Wood-fired stoneware teapot with sculpted lid finial and ash-streaked drip glaze.

works.title: Chawan tea bowls
works.description: Three wood-fired Japanese tea bowls (chawan) — sage celadon, ash-marked stoneware, and deep iron-red.

works.title: Teapot and chawan set
works.description: The wood-fired teapot displayed with a set of chawan tea bowls.

artists.name: Debra Oldman
artists.bio: Lancaster-based, Debra works across acrylic, mixed media, pastel and felting, capturing the ever-changing Morecambe Bay and the breathtaking Lakeland Fells. A first-time exhibitor this year — she came along as a friend's guest in 2024, was inspired by what she saw, and decided to submit her own work for 2026.

works.title: The Gilded Chill
works.description: Framed acrylic painting of Wastwater screes — richly textured fells in warm golds, reds and purples reflected across the lake.

artists.name: Ann Kretzschmar
artists.bio: Ann works in soft pastel, capturing the Lakeland fells, wildflower meadows and the Eskdale valley in rich, vivid colour. A returning exhibitor, she brings framed originals alongside greetings cards, coasters, keyrings and unframed prints.

works.title: Mountain Foxgloves
works.description: Foxgloves in the foreground with a fell rising beyond a lake — vivid pinks, greens and a purple-shadowed summit.

works.title: Sunflower Meadow
works.description: A sea of sunflowers stretching to dark fells under a blue sky.

works.title: Summer in Wasdale
works.description: A fell path winding through dry-stone walls toward a sunlit Lakeland summit.

works.title: Misty Morning
works.description: A misty lane with bare trees and grazing cattle, lit by a low golden sun breaking through the haze.

artists.name: Gertrude Hope
artists.bio: Gertrude's watercolours are shown in her memory, displayed by her granddaughter Ann Kretzschmar. A returning exhibitor, her work captures bridges, boats, flowers and countryside scenes in the classic English watercolour tradition.

works.title: Bakewell Bridge
works.description: A stone arch bridge over calm water, framed by summer trees — delicate washes of green and warm sandstone.

works.title: Fishing Boats
works.description: A coastal scene with a beached boat, drying nets and a boathouse, hills receding into soft haze beyond the water.

works.title: Watermill
works.description: A stone watermill with its wheel visible, set beside a rocky stream with gentle hills behind.

artists.name: Bill Walker
artists.bio: Bill works in coloured pencil, bringing British wildlife to life with extraordinary detail and warmth. A returning exhibitor, he's bringing five framed originals to Eskdale this year — foxes, hares, swans and a red squirrel, each one painstakingly rendered on toned paper.

works.title: The Fox
works.description: A fox portrait in coloured pencil on toned paper — warm russet fur, bright amber eyes and a thick ruff of white and grey.

works.title: Gazing
works.description: A tabby cat looking upward in coloured pencil on toned paper — green eyes, fine whiskers and beautifully rendered fur.

works.title: The Hare
works.description: A hare portrait in coloured pencil — alert ears, soft brown fur and a calm, watchful expression.

artists.name: Shane Stanbridge
artists.bio: Shane is a wildlife photographer originally from Hastings, East Sussex, now living in Seascale. He travels to as many different countries as possible to see and photograph as many different species as he can — so far Iceland, Norway, Finland, Bulgaria, Hungary, Sweden and Poland. He won the BBC Countryfile Judge's Favourite 2020 competition.

works.title: Red Stag
works.description: A red stag standing alert on open moorland, autumn grasses and misty fells behind.

works.title: Hare in Wild Meadowfield
works.description: A brown hare half-hidden in a meadow of crimson clover, ears up, eye bright.

works.title: Hedgehog in Pot in Autumn Leaves
works.description: A hedgehog peering out of a terracotta pot surrounded by fallen autumn leaves.

works.title: Highland Cow
works.description: A Highland cow standing on a grassy shore with a Scottish loch and mountains beyond.
